Title: [UX-001] Editor: Unified progress rail replacing dual step/tab mental model
Body:
Problem: Character builder uses numbered steps while EditorWorkspace also has tabs, creating orientation loss.
User story: As a character author, I want one progress rail with section status so I know where I am and what remains.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Shared section model drives builder and editor nav. 2. Only one primary navigation model is visible for core sections. 3. Active section, incomplete counts, blocking count, and save state are visible globally. 4. Section selection preserves edits and focuses the section heading. 5. Rail is keyboard reachable and exposes current state.
Implementation notes: Reconcile BUILDER_STEPS and EDITOR_TABS. Reuse UX-006 and UX-019 outputs.

Title: [UX-002] Editor: Sticky you-are-here breadcrumb in long sections
Body:
Problem: Long editor sections make it difficult to tell which section and subsection is being edited after scrolling.
User story: As a character editor, I want a sticky breadcrumb so I stay oriented during long editing sessions.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Breadcrumb remains visible while scrolling. 2. It shows active section and nearest subsection. 3. It includes compact completion state when available. 4. It does not cover form controls on mobile or desktop. 5. It condenses or hides when a modal requires focus.
Implementation notes: Start from current tab or forced section, then add subsection anchors.

Title: [UX-003] Builder: Build flow stages for structure, rules, card, and publish
Body:
Problem: Tree view, card view, and upload controls exist but users must infer the intended authoring order and blockers.
User story: As an ability author, I want staged flow status so I know whether to work on structure, rules, card mapping, or publish readiness.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Header shows Structure, Rules, Card, and Publish stages. 2. Each stage shows complete, warning, or blocked. 3. Users can move backward freely and forward when blockers are resolved. 4. Existing tree and card views remain available. 5. Publish disabled state names the blocking stage.
Implementation notes: Map summary warnings, invalid state, card issues, and canPublish into one stage model.

Title: [UX-004] Playmat: Explicit zone labels and turn-priority legend
Body:
Problem: Trait, surge, and action zones are visually distinctive but their combat priority can be unclear under dense states.
User story: As a player, I want persistent zone labels and a compact legend so I can identify always-on, available, and conditional cards quickly.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Trait, surge, and action zones have visible labels. 2. Legend explains ready, used, exhausted, conditional, and passive states as those states exist. 3. Labels remain readable with many cards. 4. Labels do not block hand or spotlight interactions. 5. Screen readers identify zones and card counts.
Implementation notes: Start with static labels and counts from traitCards, surgeCards, and actionCards.

Title: [UX-005] Editor: Collapse advanced controls by default
Body:
Problem: The editor exposes many controls at once, increasing scan cost for common create and edit tasks.
User story: As a newer character author, I want advanced options collapsed by default so I can complete required choices first.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Advanced controls are grouped in explicit expandable panels. 2. Required and common fields remain visible by default. 3. Collapsed panels show configured and missing-value summaries. 4. Expansion state persists during the session. 5. No editing capability is removed.
Implementation notes: Candidate areas include origin details, archetype boons, optional goal metadata, and dense potential or perk controls.

Title: [UX-006] Editor: Live section summary cards
Body:
Problem: Users lack a compact view of completion, missing choices, and section-level blockers while building a character.
User story: As a character editor, I want live section summaries so I can see what is complete and jump to missing inputs.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Each primary section exposes counts, missing values, and blocking issues. 2. Summary items link or scroll to relevant inputs. 3. Summaries update immediately when sheet state changes. 4. Data is reusable by progress rail, breadcrumb, and readiness panel. 5. Empty or unknown states are explicit.
Implementation notes: Build a pure summary derivation layer before wiring UI.

Title: [UX-007] Builder: Pinned blocking validation panel
Body:
Problem: Rule and card issues exist but can be hidden inside sidebar modes or view-specific regions.
User story: As an ability author, I want blocking validation pinned at the top so I always know the next issue to fix.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Blocking issues are visible in tree and card views. 2. Issues are grouped by blocking, warning, and note. 3. Each issue provides a target action. 4. Panel collapses to a ready state when there are no blockers. 5. Publish uses the same severity model.
Implementation notes: Use summary warnings, budget warnings, card issues, and publish guards as inputs.

Title: [UX-008] Playmat: Ready-now versus situational card states
Body:
Problem: Cards with different timing or reset requirements can appear equally usable during combat.
User story: As a player, I want ready-now and situational card states so I can identify usable options without rereading every card.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Cards show ready, conditional, passive, used, and unavailable states. 2. Users can filter or sort by state without losing current detail context. 3. State model accounts for action economy and reset condition. 4. Badges have accessible names and do not rely on color alone. 5. Default, custom, trait, surge, action, and Recollect cards are classified.
Implementation notes: Establish the shared playmat card state model for later turn-state work.

Title: [UX-009] Editor: Bulk skill and proficiency operations
Body:
Problem: Repetitive skill and proficiency edits are slow when users tune many selections.
User story: As a character editor, I want bulk add, remove, and reset operations so repeated changes are fast and recoverable.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Users can select multiple skills or proficiencies. 2. Bulk add, remove, and reset are supported. 3. Destructive changes show a confirmation summary. 4. Latest bulk operation is undoable. 5. Validation prevents illegal duplicates or blocked selections.
Implementation notes: Use existing command-layer functions where possible and update save state immediately.

Title: [UX-010] Editor: Inline quick-edit chips for common fields
Body:
Problem: Frequent edits require reopening dense sections or modal flows.
User story: As a returning editor, I want inline quick-edit chips so common identity, origin, and archetype changes take only a few interactions.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Summary cards expose quick-edit chips for high-frequency fields. 2. Chips open the smallest viable control. 3. Common edits are possible in no more than two interactions after the field is visible. 4. Changes update section controls and summaries. 5. Quick edits follow modal and focus rules.
Implementation notes: Start with name, origin facet names, selected origin skill, active archetypes, and bloodline ability.

Title: [UX-011] Builder: Keyboard-first node creation palette search
Body:
Problem: Graph authoring depends on precision drag and drop, slowing expert users and blocking keyboard-only users.
User story: As an ability author, I want searchable node creation so I can add blocks without dragging.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Command palette opens from a button and shortcut. 2. Palette search covers name, category, and related rule terms. 3. Selected item inserts near selected node, viewport center, or target cursor. 4. New node becomes selected and announced. 5. Existing drag path remains available.
Implementation notes: Reuse buildPaletteSections as the source of searchable items.

Title: [UX-012] Builder: Snap, grid alignment, and auto-layout suggestions
Body:
Problem: Ability graphs can become visually noisy and hard to edit as node count grows.
User story: As an ability author, I want layout aids so I can keep the graph readable without manual positioning work.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Nodes can snap to a visible grid. 2. Tidy layout preserves nodes, links, and selected context. 3. Larger graphs can preview layout before applying. 4. Undo restores previous layout. 5. Layout does not alter ability rules or card data.
Implementation notes: Evaluate React Flow helpers or a directed graph layout library before custom layout code.

Title: [UX-013] Playmat: Pin active card without spotlight modal
Body:
Problem: Spotlight is useful for detail but modal context switching is awkward when tracking active turn state.
User story: As a player, I want to pin my active card so it remains visible while I continue using the playmat.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Any action, surge, or trait can be pinned and unpinned. 2. Pinned card remains visible while zones remain interactive. 3. Pin state persists during the current turn until reset. 4. Spotlight still opens without losing pin state. 5. Keyboard users can pin, unpin, and navigate pinned-card focus.
Implementation notes: Add a pinned-card region distinct from spotlight modal state.

Title: [UX-014] Playmat: Explicit one-click face toggle affordance
Body:
Problem: Face toggling is present but easy to miss, especially on tray cards.
User story: As a player, I want an obvious face toggle so I can flip attack and movement faces without opening the card.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Two-sided cards show a persistent flip control. 2. Control is keyboard reachable and labels the next face. 3. Tray and spotlight previews stay consistent. 4. Control is large enough for touch. 5. Single-face cards do not show misleading controls.
Implementation notes: Build on existing toggleCardFace and toggleSpotlightFace behavior.

Title: [UX-015] Editor: First-run guided checklist by section
Body:
Problem: New users must infer a valid character completion path from dense controls and external rules knowledge.
User story: As a first-time author, I want a guided checklist so I can complete a valid character without leaving the builder.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Checklist items are grouped by editor section. 2. Each item explains the decision and links to the input. 3. Completed items update live. 4. Users can dismiss and reopen the checklist. 5. Checklist works in create and edit contexts.
Implementation notes: Use readiness and summary derivations instead of duplicate validation rules.

Title: [UX-016] Builder: Interactive starter templates by intent
Body:
Problem: Blank presets help, but users still need to know which blocks create common ability shapes.
User story: As an ability author, I want templates by intent so I can start from common melee, spell, support, defensive, or utility patterns.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Template picker includes melee, ranged, spell, support, defensive, and utility options. 2. Applying a template creates graph nodes, rule selections, and card defaults. 3. Users can preview template summary. 4. Applying to a non-empty graph requires confirmation and is undoable. 5. Templates work with staged flow.
Implementation notes: Extend the existing Blank Action and Blank Surge preset concept.

Title: [UX-017] Builder: Contextual helper text for empty and invalid states
Body:
Problem: Empty and invalid states may identify missing data but not explain what to do next.
User story: As an ability author, I want contextual helper text so I can recover from invalid states without guessing.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Empty palette, inspector, graph, inventory, and card inspector states offer next actions. 2. Invalid states include remediation links when targets are known. 3. Helper text uses validation-panel language. 4. Guidance does not appear as a blocking error unless it is blocking. 5. Screen readers receive the same guidance.
Implementation notes: Target BuilderSidebar empty inspector and card issue regions first.

Title: [UX-018] Playmat: Dismissible playmat coach marks
Body:
Problem: The playmat has custom zone, flip, spotlight, and Recollect interactions that are not obvious on first use.
User story: As a first-time playmat user, I want brief coach marks so I can learn key interactions without external documentation.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Coach marks appear once per user or browser profile. 2. They identify zones, flipping, spotlight, and Recollect when applicable. 3. Users can dismiss and reopen them. 4. Coach marks do not block critical play controls. 5. They respect reduced motion settings.
Implementation notes: Store dismissal in local storage unless a preference store already exists.

Title: [UX-019] Editor: Explicit save timeline with retry
Body:
Problem: Basic save states do not give enough confidence during long editing sessions or failures.
User story: As a character editor, I want explicit save timeline feedback so I know whether changes are saved and can retry failures.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Header shows saving, saved, unsaved, offline, and error states. 2. Saved state includes last saved time when available. 3. Error state includes retry and failure text. 4. Save status is not hidden behind view-character affordance. 5. Status changes are announced politely.
Implementation notes: CharacterBuilderShell already receives saveState but may need richer metadata.

Title: [UX-020] Editor: Unsaved-change guard before route leave
Body:
Problem: Users can leave long editing sessions without a clear warning when edits are pending or save failed.
User story: As a character editor, I want a guard before leaving with unsaved changes so I do not lose work accidentally.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Route changes, browser unload, and view-sheet transitions detect unsaved edits. 2. Prompt appears only for pending edits or save error. 3. Users can stay, discard, or retry save when supported. 4. No prompt appears when saved. 5. Tests cover pending, saved, and error states.
Implementation notes: Share state with UX-019 to avoid duplicate save models.

Title: [UX-021] Builder: Publish preflight panel
Body:
Problem: Upload readiness is spread across disabled button state, tooltips, and distributed rule or card errors.
User story: As an ability author, I want a publish preflight panel so I understand what will publish and what must be fixed first.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Panel lists blocking issues, warnings, notes, and data quality checks. 2. Publish is blocked only by blocking issues. 3. Issues link to graph, card, or metadata targets. 4. Panel summarizes title, kind, action economy, reset, cost, and visibility. 5. Publish shows sending, success, retryable error, and non-retryable error states.
Implementation notes: Reuse severity from UX-007 and feed UX-003 stages.

Title: [UX-022] Builder: Post-upload success path
Body:
Problem: Successful upload confirms publication but does not clearly guide users to view, assign, or continue editing.
User story: As an ability author, I want success actions after upload so I can take the next useful step.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Success state includes view in library and assign to character when id is available. 2. Success state names whether local changes remain unpublished. 3. Users can dismiss messaging without losing published id. 4. Success actions are keyboard reachable. 5. Error state remains visually distinct.
Implementation notes: Expand the current publishResult region in BuilderWorkspace.

Title: [UX-023] Playmat: Recollect modal validation hints
Body:
Problem: Recollect assignments can be invalid or confusing without inline feedback before apply.
User story: As a player resolving Recollect, I want validation hints per assignment so I can fix mistakes before applying.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Each row shows valid, duplicate, unavailable, or unchanged status. 2. Apply is disabled only when assignment cannot be applied. 3. Invalid reasons are inline and screen-reader accessible. 4. Users can reset to recommended layout. 5. Missing potential or missing perks show actionable guidance.
Implementation notes: Reuse getRecollectFaceOptions, getSelectedRecollectFaces, and potential lookup logic.

Title: [UX-024] Playmat: Action-use feedback and cooldown badges
Body:
Problem: After use, cards do not clearly show spent, cooldown, or reset status for the current turn.
User story: As a player, I want immediate action-use feedback so I can track what is spent and what resets next.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Users can mark actions and surges as used. 2. Used cards update visually immediately. 3. Reset and cooldown badges use ability document reset condition where available. 4. Users can reset all turn state from a clear control. 5. State changes are keyboard accessible and reversible during the turn.
Implementation notes: Define local turn-state first, then decide whether persistence is needed.

Title: [UX-025] All: Full keyboard traversal for critical workflows
Body:
Problem: Critical editor, builder, graph, card, and playmat workflows still rely on mouse-optimized paths.
User story: As a keyboard-only user, I want to create, edit, publish, and play without a mouse.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Critical workflows can be completed by keyboard. 2. Keyboard order follows visual workflow order. 3. Shortcuts are discoverable through accessible controls. 4. Focus is never trapped except inside active modals. 5. QA scripts cover critical keyboard paths.
Implementation notes: Split implementation tasks by surface after an accessibility inventory.

Title: [UX-026] All: Modal focus management improvements
Body:
Problem: Multiple modal workflows need reliable focus entry, trap, escape, and return behavior.
User story: As a keyboard or assistive technology user, I want modal focus handled consistently so I return to the invoking control.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Opening a modal focuses title or first meaningful control. 2. Closing returns focus to invoking control when it exists. 3. Escape closes dismissible modals consistently. 4. Background content is not reachable while modal is open. 5. Origin picker, archetype modal, spotlight, and Recollect modal are covered.
Implementation notes: Consider a shared modal primitive before patching each modal.

Title: [UX-027] All: Color contrast hardening for critical UI states
Body:
Problem: Low-opacity labels, badges, and status text can reduce readability in dense surfaces.
User story: As a user with low vision or challenging display conditions, I want critical UI to meet contrast standards.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Critical text, labels, buttons, badges, errors, and selected states meet WCAG AA. 2. Disabled controls remain distinguishable. 3. Severity does not rely on color alone. 4. Editor, builder, and playmat CSS modules are included. 5. A contrast check is attached before closure.
Implementation notes: Audit CSS modules for low-opacity text and badge colors.

Title: [UX-028] Builder/Playmat: Non-visual labels for icon-only controls
Body:
Problem: Icon-only and symbol-only controls need consistent names for screen readers and tooltips.
User story: As an assistive technology user, I want every icon-only control to have a non-visual label so I know what action it performs.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Every icon-only or symbol-only builder and playmat control has an aria-label or text equivalent. 2. Changing-state controls include target state when useful. 3. Tooltips or titles explain unfamiliar icons. 4. Accessibility checks confirm no unnamed critical controls remain. 5. Labels use product vocabulary consistently.
Implementation notes: Prioritize toolbar, face toggles, spotlight, and playmat zone actions.

Title: [UX-029] Editor: Mobile section chunking and sticky action row
Body:
Problem: High-density editor forms are difficult to scan and operate on small screens.
User story: As a mobile character editor, I want chunked sections and sticky actions so I can edit without losing navigation or save controls.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Sections are chunked into mobile-friendly subsections. 2. Save status, section navigation, and primary action remain reachable. 3. Controls avoid horizontal overflow. 4. Modals and pickers fit mobile viewports. 5. Mobile QA covers all editor sections.
Implementation notes: Follow UX-001 instead of adding a separate mobile nav model.

Title: [UX-030] Builder: Adaptive single-column mode under 1100px
Body:
Problem: Builder split layout can crowd graph, sidebar, card view, and toolbar on medium and small screens.
User story: As an ability author on a smaller screen, I want an adaptive layout so palette, inspector, graph, and card view remain reachable.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Under 1100px, sidebar and workspace adapt to single-column or collapsible rails. 2. Palette, inspector, stage status, graph, and card view remain reachable. 3. Toolbars wrap or condense without overlap. 4. React Flow controls remain usable. 5. No horizontal overflow at 1100px, 900px, 760px, and 390px.
Implementation notes: Preserve workflow order from UX-003.

Title: [UX-031] Playmat: Small-screen tactical list/grid mode
Body:
Problem: Fan overlap and stacked previews can reduce card readability on small screens.
User story: As a mobile player, I want a tactical list or grid mode so I can read and use abilities during play.
Acceptance criteria: 1. At small breakpoints, action fan is replaced by readable list or grid. 2. Ready, used, conditional, and pinned states remain visible. 3. Face toggles and detail actions are touch friendly. 4. Trait and surge zones remain distinct. 5. QA confirms no overlap or inaccessible controls below 760px.
Implementation notes: Build on UX-008 card state and UX-024 turn tracking.

Title: [UX-032] Playmat: Gesture-safe tap targets and spacing pass
Body:
Problem: Dense tray and card controls can be difficult to tap accurately on compact screens.
User story: As a touch user, I want comfortable tap targets and spacing so I can use cards without accidental activation.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Critical tap targets meet agreed minimum size. 2. Adjacent destructive or state-changing controls have safe spacing. 3. Card preview, face toggle, pin, use, and close controls are included. 4. Text does not overlap after spacing changes. 5. Compact viewports are tested.
Implementation notes: Apply after UX-031 establishes compact layout shape.

Title: [UX-033] Editor: Character readiness panel
Body:
Problem: The editor lacks a consolidated readiness view for publish-ready or play-ready character state.
User story: As a character author, I want a readiness panel so I can resolve missing origin boons, invalid levels, missing abilities, and other blockers before play.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Panel summarizes completion by section and overall readiness. 2. Blocking, warning, and optional polish items are separated. 3. Items link to relevant sections or controls. 4. Readiness derives from domain rules or shared summaries. 5. Panel works from builder and editor entry points.
Implementation notes: Make this the authoritative character validation surface for UX-015 and UX-035.

Title: [UX-034] Builder: Ability ownership and visibility status in header
Body:
Problem: Authors need to know whether an ability is draft, personal, public, admin, or constrained before publishing or assigning it.
User story: As an ability author, I want ownership and visibility status in the header so I understand where the ability will be available.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Header shows draft/published and visibility or ownership status when known. 2. Status feeds publish preflight once available. 3. Unknown status is explicit and non-blocking. 4. Status text is accessible and high contrast. 5. Status updates after successful publish.
Implementation notes: Start with local draft and published states if repository visibility is not available.

Title: [UX-035] Builder/Editor: Direct assign-to-character flow after publish
Body:
Problem: Publishing an ability and using it on a character are separate workflows, forcing manual search or id transfer.
User story: As an ability author, I want to assign a published ability directly to a character so I can test and play it quickly.
Acceptance criteria: 1. After publish, users can open assign-to-character from success state. 2. Flow lists eligible characters and assignment blockers. 3. Assignment adds ability without manual id entry. 4. Success links to the character sheet playmat. 5. Failures distinguish permissions, validation, network, or missing data.
Implementation notes: Use publishResult id and character readiness blockers from UX-033.

Title: [UX-036] Playmat: Shareable loadout snapshot
Body:
Problem: Players and GMs have limited support for comparing or sharing a selected ability set for planning.
User story: As a player or GM, I want to export and import a loadout snapshot so party planning does not require rebuilding selections manually.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Export includes ability ids and relevant local playmat state. 2. Import previews unresolved or unavailable abilities before applying. 3. Export avoids private character details not required for planning. 4. Import requires confirmation before overwrite. 5. Snapshot format includes a version field.
Implementation notes: Treat snapshot as planning data, not authoritative persistence.

Title: [UX-037] Editor: Skeleton placeholders for pickers and transitions
Body:
Problem: Async pickers and section transitions can show blank or abrupt states, reducing perceived reliability.
User story: As a character editor, I want loading placeholders so I can tell the app is working while picker data or section UI loads.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Origin picker loading states show skeleton or structured placeholders. 2. Section transitions preserve layout dimensions where possible. 3. Loading, empty, and error states use UX-040 language. 4. Placeholders do not steal focus. 5. Loading state is accessible to screen readers.
Implementation notes: Start with originPickerLoading, originPickerError, and originPickerRows states.

Title: [UX-038] Builder: Progressive loading for graph and card assets
Body:
Problem: Heavy graph, card, and rendering assets can delay interaction on the builder surface.
User story: As an ability author, I want the builder to become interactive progressively so I can start before non-critical assets finish loading.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Critical toolbar and stage status render before non-critical assets when feasible. 2. Graph and card areas show stable loading and retry states. 3. Non-critical previews are deferred until visible. 4. Interaction readiness has an agreed latency target. 5. Loading changes do not break import, export, or publish.
Implementation notes: Evaluate code splitting and lazy rendering around card canvas and React Flow.

Title: [UX-039] Playmat: Card prefetch and fast spotlight transitions
Body:
Problem: Spotlight detail should feel immediate because card inspection is core during play.
User story: As a player, I want spotlight detail to open quickly so I can inspect cards without slowing the turn.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Spotlight-needed card data is prefetched where practical. 2. Spotlight opens within the agreed latency budget. 3. Animation respects reduced motion. 4. Loading fallback appears if detail cannot render immediately. 5. Prefetch does not block initial playmat interaction.
Implementation notes: Coordinate with UX-013 so performance supports pinned-card and spotlight surfaces.

Title: [UX-040] All: Latency messaging standards
Body:
Problem: Async paths use inconsistent language such as loading, sending, upload, retry, or blank states.
User story: As a user, I want consistent latency and error messaging so I understand what is happening and what I can do next.
Acceptance criteria: 1. Copy standards define loading, saving, publishing, retrying, offline, empty, and error language. 2. Editor, builder, and playmat async states use the standard. 3. Every error state includes a next action when one exists. 4. Loading messages avoid implying success before completion. 5. Accessibility announcements match visible status.
Implementation notes: Ship as a small copy and component pass, then keep as checklist for future UX work.
